6.2.m: Then, seeing the enraged troop of mothers crushing the great asuras,
and seeing his army turned back, Vajra then released an illusion,
named Tāmasī, difficult to overcome, by which the maidens were bewildered.
When it had become darkness, that goddess, overwhelmed with fear,
came along with them to the supreme Mahākālavana,
where Hara, holding a skull, was stationed in the form of a liṅga.
Having learned that the troop of mothers had fled due to the power of that illusion,
and Vajra also knowing that the thirty [gods] were residing together with the goddess,
he came to that place surrounded by his own army.
In the divine Mahākālavana, surrounded by hundreds of millions of chariots,

Meanwhile, Nārada, the best of sages,
arrived full of eagerness at the beautiful cave on Mount Mandara.
He told the Lord of the defeat of the gods by Vajra:
“O God, the thirty [gods] have been struck down in the Mahākālavana, O Lord,
by Vajra, the son of Ruru; therefore, go forth, O Maheśvara!”
Having heard the words of Nārada, then I, O supreme goddess,
came swiftly from Mandara, having assumed a most terrible form,
surrounded by gaṇas, with flashing, extremely fierce and dreadful serpents.
In front was seen the great army of the dānavas, terrifying to behold.
Mahākālavana was besieged on all sides by the asura,
by Vajra, the son of Ruru, who was irresistible, O renowned lady.

Then all the hosts of gods, their minds filled with overflowing joy,
bowed down to that mighty son of Ruru.
Because of the majesty of this god, the mighty Vajra was burnt
along with his army; therefore, from that, this [god], Ḍamarukeśvara,

If with devotion, even by chance, men dedicated to sin
behold the liṅga Ḍamarukeśvara standing in this place,
even they will surely go to the eternal world of Rudra.

Śrī Rudra said:
Know the fifth god to be Anādikalpeśvara, O Pārvatī,
destroyer of all sins, eternal; he is ever sung of as beginningless.
At the beginning of the kalpa in ancient times, O goddess, this liṅga emerged,

From this liṅga arose the universe, both unmoving and moving,
and in time it dissolves into this liṅga, O daughter of the mountain.
From this liṅga arose the lineages of divine seers and ancestors,
the manvantaras, the genealogies, and the deeds of their descendants;
as many creations as there are, and as many dissolutions;
the oceans, mountains, rivers, and forests;

All that is visible and invisible [arose] from this liṅga, O fair-faced one.
That which is the beginningless cause, which the great seers call the unmanifest,

At the end of the dissolution, this entire divine [reality] existed by it.
I, awakened on the earth, the origin of the world, having no beginning,
the cause of all, incomprehensible in self, supreme, extraordinary, transcending actions,
swiftly manifesting Prakṛti and Puruṣa, the Lord of the universe,
the Supreme Lord, agitated them through supreme yoga.
Just as fragrance causes an agitation merely by its presence,
without acting directly upon the mind, so that Supreme Lord,
the beginningless God, is spoken of as the supreme cause of the world.

6.2.m: He alone was formerly the agitator, and he the agitated, the sovereign of the earth.
Through contraction and expansion, he remains in the state of the primordial matter.
He, the Lord of the universe, though devoid of qualities, manifests quality of passion;
experiencing it and attaining the nature of Brahmā, he initiates creation.
In the nature of Brahmā he creates the worlds; then, through the predominance of goodness,
attaining the nature of Viṣṇu, he preserves them according to dharma.
Then, moved by the quality of darkness, in the nature of Rudra, having withdrawn the entire universe,
the three worlds, he indeed sleeps—the possessor of the three qualities, yet devoid of qualities.
Just as the same field-owner is first called a sower, then a protector, and then a reaper,
and acquires those names accordingly, so it is with the states of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra.
In the nature of Brahmā he creates the worlds, and in that of Rudra he destroys them;
in the nature of Viṣṇu he protects them all. These three states are always remembered:

6.2.m: The venerable Mahādeva said: / Know Svarṇajvāleśvara as the sixth here, O glorious lady, / by the mere darśana of which one becomes wealthy in this world. // Formerly, O goddess, while I was sporting with you in my dwelling, / a hundred divine years passed as I relished sole delight in lovemaking. // Then fire was dispatched by all the gods into my presence; / thereupon Fire arrived for the sake of the three worlds, O glorious lady. // Then my semen was cast into the mouth of Fire by me as I sported; / burning from it then, Fire went to the Gaṅgā. // Having gone there, Fire cast forth the semen, so exceedingly difficult to bear; / nevertheless, Fire was still burned by the remainder of the semen, O Pārvatī. // Then, from that remainder of the semen, lovely and divine gold was born, / blazing with excessive heat, unbearable and hard to retain, O dear one. // Seeing that first offspring of Fire born, O Pārvatī, / overcome by greed, the asuras, the suras, the gandharvas and kinnaras, // the yakṣas, sādhyas, and piśācas, humans, rākṣasas, and birds, / rushed forward in great fury, desiring to seize the gold. // For the sake of the gold, a great roar arose from those clamoring, “This is mine!” / And out of ignorance a battle arose that took many lives. // Then, seizing foremost shields and diverse weapons, / they roared with great sounds along with the gods, O glorious lady: // asuras with asuras, humans with humans, / gandharvas with gandharvas, kinnaras with kinnaras, // spirits with spirits, and rākṣasas with rākṣasas, / vetālas with vetālas fought an exceedingly dreadful battle. // Son hated father, and father likewise hated son; / wife struck down her husband, and husband likewise his dear wife. // Son killed his own mother, and mother harmed her son; / then an unyielding hostility arose on account of the gold, // most horrific and great among gods and asuras all alike. / Broad and sharp javelins fell by the thousands, // along with extremely sharp-pointed iron bars and various weapons. // For the sake of the gold, O great goddess, vomiting much blood, // swords, spears, clubs, and rṛṣṭi-daggers fell upon the surface of the earth; / and heads were severed in the terrible battle by battleaxes. // With their limbs smeared with blood and having slain one another, / they lay like peaks of mountains rich in mineral ores. // A cry of “Alas! Alas!” arose by the thousands, causing terror, / as they cut each other down with weapons for the sake of the gold. // With iron bludgeons, nooses, and fists like vajras, / as they struck one another in battle, the sound seemed to touch the sky. // “Cut! Pierce! Run! Knock down! Attack!”— / such exceedingly horrific cries were heard there on every side. // Thus, while this tumultuous and terrifying battle was taking place, / the earth trembled, O goddess, and the gods, along with Indra, were terrified. // The oceans grew agitated and the mountains moved; / for the sake of it, the entire world, with gods, asuras, and humans, was tormented. // The seers, headed by the Vālakhilyas, the gods, with Śakra at their head, / placing Bṛhaspati at the fore, and the women went to Brahmā's realm. // Panting for breath, with their heads battered and shattered, / they recounted in full the entire event that was destroying the three worlds. // Hearing their speech, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, / having reflected, came into my presence along with them. // They were all questioned by me: “By whom have you been battered? / By whom have you been afflicted with weapons and missiles? Whence has fear come upon you? // And who is this wicked dānava by whom you have been so severely tormented?” / Then all was recounted before me, O goddess, by those overwhelmed with fear. // The gods, headed by Brahmā, then told me the cause of their fear: // “We are all ruined out of greed and on account of gold; / and the entire world, with gods, asuras, and humans, is tormented.” // Hearing their words, O fair-faced lady, I understood / that a horrific strife among one another had indeed arisen for its sake, // by which the destruction of the three worlds was swiftly wrought. / One on whose account life is surrendered is called a slayer of a brahmin; // the son of Fire is indeed a slayer of a brahmin, on whose account people died. / His body will become variegated and deformed; // minerals shall indeed arise in his body, there is no doubt. / Incomparable suffering is foreseen—cutting, burning, rubbing, and the like. // In the meantime, Fire, having seen the behavior of his son / and having realized my anger, was terrified on account of his son. // He came into my presence along with the gold, O goddess; / indeed, I was propitiated by Fire for the sake of his son, O fair-faced lady: // “This son of yours, O Śaṃkara, must be protected by you, O god; / place him in your own treasury, O supreme lord! // When you are pleased, O Mahādeva, he can be obtained—of this there is no doubt; / let him be given at your pleasure to whichever person you will, O goddess!” // Hearing this speech of his, who is the mouth of the ancestors and the gods, / “So be it,” was promised by me out of desire, O glorious lady.

6.2.m:
Out of affection, the son of Fire was then placed by me upon my lap;
out of affection, he was kissed on the head and embraced again and again:
“I grant you a boon, O fortunate one; choose an auspicious boon!
I am exceedingly pleased; obtain whatever you desire as you wish!
I instruct you, and thus you shall attain the highest good:
There is a place upon the surface of the earth that fulfills my desires,
imperishable at the dissolution of the world, O son—the auspicious Mahākālavana.
Right there, to the south of Karkoṭaka, is a liṅga
that removes great sin, O son, and bestows radiance upon darśana.
By the mere darśana of it, you will have accomplished all your ends.”
And he shall become meritorious through the purifier, and hard to attain;
a base-born man shall become noble, and an impure man pure;
and the deformed shall become handsome by your grace.
Gifts, religious observances, and restrictions,
sacrifices, fasts, sacred fords, piṇḍa offerings, and the like,
shall all become completely fulfilled through the gift of you, O one of good vows.

You shall exercise sovereignty over all precious stones,
and you shall be dear and beloved to the gods and the worlds.
Addressed thus, O great goddess, O lovely-faced one, possessing a celestial form,
surrounded by a garland of flames, he became meritorious and pure indeed.
The gold was addressed by the liṅga: "By good fortune, by good fortune!"—[and was told:] "Gold,
from this day forth you shall attain fame on the surface of the earth by that name.
You must always remain near me, O son of fire!
Your fame shall be imperishable in the three worlds."
Addressed thus by the liṅga, O goddess, the son of fire became exceedingly pure,
his body encircled by flames, equal in splendor to ten million suns.
Radiance filled with a garland of flames was then obtained by the gold;
therefore, O goddess, Śiva is renowned as Svarṇajvāleśvara.
Whoever worships that Śiva, Svarṇajvāleśvara, with devotion,
to him, O goddess, victory and a mighty kingdom accrue,
as well as lordship, the capacity to give gifts, and endless sons and grandsons.

Whatever fruit a man obtains by the offering of piṇḍas at Gayā,

are constantly honored by Lakṣmī, who fulfills their desires.

Formerly, in the Vārāha Kalpa, the spotless celestial seer Nārada,
desiring to see Śatakratu, went to heaven, O goddess.
There, in a delightful garden grove adorned with wish-granting trees,
everywhere filled with breezes pleasant to the touch with the fragrance of blossoms,
resounding with the sounds of vīṇās and flutes, attended by gods and Gandharvas,
illuminated by diamonds, sapphires, cat's-eye gems, moonstones, and the like,
auspicious and incomparable in qualities even to the world of Brahmā and other realms,
he saw the lord of the gods, Śatakratu, seated there,
being praised joyfully by gods, Siddhas, Cāraṇas, and Kinnaras.

related the māhātmya of the forest of Mahākāla:

to be resorted to, meritorious, pure, and the highest of sacred fords.

6.2.d: ब्रह्मा विष्णुः सहस्राक्षो वरुणो वायुरेव च ..
6.2.m: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, the thousand-eyed [Indra], Varuṇa, and Vāyu,

6.2.s: dhanadaḥ sāgarā nadyaḥ sarāṃsi sakalāni ca .. 16 ..
6.2.d: धनदः सागरा नद्यः सरांसि सकलानि च .. 16 ..
6.2.m: the Bestower of Wealth [Kubera], the oceans, rivers, and all lakes,

6.2.s: suparṇā girayo nāgāḥ sarve cākāritāḥ kratau ..
6.2.d: सुपर्णा गिरयो नागाः सर्वे चाकारिताः क्रतौ ..
6.2.m: the eagles, mountains, and serpent deities—all were invited to the rite,
along with their followers and wives, as well as brahmins who had mastered the Vedas,
great-souled brahmin-seers, and spotless celestial seers.
Having thus regarded Mahādeva as adorned with human bones
and impure—how do you dare to say:
'Let entrance be granted to me'? Especially since you are a slayer of a brahmin!"
When I was thus addressed by the brahmins, these words were spoken by me then:

6.2.s: pratīkṣyatāṃ muhūrtaṃ tu bhuktvā yāsyāmyahaṃ punaḥ .. 5.2.8.20 ..
6.2.d: प्रतीक्ष्यतां मुहूर्तं तु भुक्त्वा यास्याम्यहं पुनः .. 5.2.8.20 ..
6.2.m: "Let me wait for just a moment; having eaten, I shall go away again."

6.2.s: ityukte vacane devi tāḍito'haṃ bhṛśaṃ tadā ..
6.2.d: इत्युक्ते वचने देवि ताडितोऽहं भृशं तदा ..
6.2.m: When these words were spoken, O goddess, I was violently struck then
with clods of earth, with sticks, with feet, and repeatedly with fists.

6.2.s: atha prahasya tatkṣiptvā tāṃ vediṃ darbhasaṃstṛtām ..
6.2.d: अथ प्रहस्य तत्क्षिप्त्वा तां वेदिं दर्भसंस्तृताम् ..
6.2.m: Then, laughing, having thrown that [skull] upon the altar strewn with darbha grass,
I disappeared like the lamp of a skull [being snuffed out], unnoticed by the best of the twice-born.
When I had vanished, that skull was thrown outside the sacrificial pavilion.
Then another of the same form arose there, O glorious one!
Thus hundreds of thousands, millions, and tens of millions
were thrown away and yet appeared there; thereupon they were filled with amazement.
Then all the wise ones said: "This is not the doing of anyone else,
except the god Mahādeva, who bears the Gaṅgā and the crescent moon upon his crest!"

6.2.s: tato'haṃ vividhaiḥ stotraiḥ stuto vipraiḥ pṛthakpṛthak ..
6.2.d: ततोऽहं विविधैः स्तोत्रैः स्तुतो विप्रैः पृथक्पृथक् ..
6.2.m: Then I was praised by the brahmins individually with various hymns of praise,

6.2.s: homaṃ cakruśca te vahnau maṃtraiśca śatarudriyeḥ .. 26 ..
6.2.d: होमं चक्रुश्च ते वह्नौ मंत्रैश्च शतरुद्रियेः .. 26 ..
6.2.m: and they made oblations into the fire with the mantras of the Śatarudrīya.
I was pleased then, O goddess, out of compassion for the twice-born [and said]:
"Choose, O all brahmins, whatever boon is desired in your heart!"
Then those brahmins said: "Because of our ignorance, violence was done
against you; thereby the sin of killing a brahmin was incurred by us, O Lord of the universe!
For the destruction of that sin of killing a brahmin, grant us your favor, O Lord!"
We choose indeed this boon, no other desired boon." // 29
And then he spoke this before those twice-born:
"Where the heap of skulls was placed on earth by you, // 30
there was a beginningless liṅga hidden by the turning of time.
Let the brahmins behold that liṅga, which brings deliverance from the killing of a brahmin! // 31

6.2.s: kṛtā mayāpi vipreṃdrā brahmahatyā svayaṃ purā ..
6.2.d: कृता मयापि विप्रेंद्रा ब्रह्महत्या स्वयं पुरा ..
6.2.m: Even by me, O best of brahmins, the killing of a brahmin was committed myself formerly,
severing the fifth head of Brahmā, which was fierce with radiance. // 32
Thereupon the sin of killing a brahmin arose, extremely unbearable to me,

6.2.s: kapālaṃ ca kare lagnaṃ tathā cātīva duḥsaham.. 33 ..
6.2.d: कपालं च करे लग्नं तथा चातीव दुःसहम्.. 33 ..
6.2.m: and the skull adhered to my hand, likewise most unbearable. // 33
Then, burning and enveloped indeed by the killing of a brahmin,
I went quickly on a journey for my own purpose to destroy it. // 34

6.2.s: gataḥ sarveṣu tīrtheṣu naiva muktastu hatyayā ..
6.2.d: गतः सर्वेषु तीर्थेषु नैव मुक्तस्तु हत्यया ..
6.2.m: I went to all the sacred fords, yet was not freed from the murder;

6.2.s: tato duḥkhī susaṃtapto naiva lebhe sukhaṃ kvacita .. 35 ..
6.2.d: ततो दुःखी सुसंतप्तो नैव लेभे सुखं क्वचित .. 35 ..
6.2.m: then, sorrowful and sorely tormented, I found no happiness anywhere. // 35
In the meantime, a divine bodiless voice said:

6.2.s: gacchāvantīṃ svayaṃ nātha kimarthaṃ khidyate vṛthā .. 36 ..
6.2.d: गच्छावन्तीं स्वयं नाथ किमर्थं खिद्यते वृथा .. 36 ..
6.2.m: 'Go to Avantī yourself, O Lord; why grieve in vain? // 36
The holy Mahākālavana was created by you, O Lord,
the station of the skull-handed one, Rudra, wondrous to behold;
how do you not know the sacred field that destroys great sins? // 37
In that sacred field there is a great liṅga near Gajarūpa;
behold it, O Lord of the gods, [and] the killing of a brahmin will vanish.' // 38
Then I came swiftly, having heard that excellent speech;
the great liṅga was beheld by me, situated with a skull in hand. // 39
Then, O brahmins, the skull fell to the ground from my hand;
'This is the god Kapāleśvara'—thus was the name given by me. // 40
Let the brahmins behold that god named Kapāleśvara,
by the mere sight of whom you will become free from stain." // 41
Then the liṅga was beheld by them, surrounded by many skulls;
they became fulfilled in their purpose from the sight of that liṅga. // 42
Therefore it became famous on earth by the name Kapāleśvara.
Those who worship the one named Kapāleśvara, O great goddess, // 43

6.2.s: kṛtapuṇyā narā devi te yāṃti paramaṃ padam ..
6.2.d: कृतपुण्या नरा देवि ते यांति परमं पदम् ..
6.2.m: those men having acquired merit, O goddess, go to the supreme abode.
Even having committed a terrible sin, the killing of a brahmin and the like, a man— // 44

6.2.s: tatpāpaṃ vilayaṃ yāti liṃgasyāsya ca darśanāt ..
6.2.d: तत्पापं विलयं याति लिंगस्यास्य च दर्शनात् ..
6.2.m: that sin dissolves through the sight of this liṅga.
Whatever sin has been amassed by deed, mind, or speech,
this god destroys it when worshipped on the fourteenth [tithi]. // 45
Those who perform worship even incidentally, O fair-faced lady,
they too will attain whatever desires, even those very hard to obtain:
incomparable lordship and virtue, long life, freedom from disease, // 46
unmatched freedom from rivals, and whatever else [they wish], one will obtain.

6.2.s: atīva pāpino ye ca krūrakarmaratā narāḥ .. 47 ..
6.2.d: अतीव पापिनो ये च क्रूरकर्मरता नराः .. 47 ..
6.2.m: And men who are exceedingly sinful and engaged in cruel acts // 47
will become free from sin and leaders of my gaṇas, O dear one.

6.2.s: niyamena prapaśyaṃti ye devaṃ vatsaraṃ priye ..
6.2.d: नियमेन प्रपश्यंति ये देवं वत्सरं प्रिये ..
6.2.m: Those who regularly behold the god for a year, O dear one,

6.2.s: te paśyaṃti tanuṃ tyaktvā madīyaṃ bhavanaṃ priyam .. 48 ..
6.2.d: ते पश्यंति तनुं त्यक्त्वा मदीयं भवनं प्रियम् .. 48 ..
6.2.m: leaving their body, behold my beloved abode. // 48

6.2.s: eṣa te kathito devi prabhāvaḥ pāpanāśanaḥ ..
6.2.d: एष ते कथितो देवि प्रभावः पापनाशनः ..
6.2.m: This power of the god Kapāleśvara that destroys sin has been declared to you, O goddess;
now hear of Svargadvāreśvara. // 49

6.2.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvaṃtyakhaṇḍe caturaśītiliṃgamāhātmye kapāleśvaramāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāmāṣṭamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 8 ..
6.2.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवंत्यखण्डे चतुरशीतिलिंगमाहात्म्ये कपालेश्वरमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनामाष्टमोऽध्यायः .. 8 ..
6.2.m: Thus ends the eighth chapter, titled 'Description of the Glory of Kapāleśvara' in the Eighty-Four Liṅgas Praise in the fifth section, Avantīkhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skandapurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. // 8

6.2.m: The venerable Rudra said: / Know the ninth liṅga to be Svargadvāreśvara, O Pārvatī, / which removes all sins, O goddess, and bestows heaven and liberation as its fruit. / When those sisters, beginning with Aśvinī, came / to the supreme mountain Kailāsa, O goddess, they were filled with wonder upon seeing you: / 'We have been invited to the sacrifice together with our husbands and retinues / out of affection by our father, O goddess, with great honour. / Were you remembered, O large-eyed one, or did father forget you? / For what reason were you not invited by our father?' / Hearing those words of theirs, you, out of dishonour, / then gave up your life-breaths through yoga before them, O Pārvatī. / Then, burning with grief, they went to where the lord of creatures was / and reported the whole incident before Dakṣa just as it had happened. / Hearing those terrible words, Dakṣa said nothing at all. / When I saw you fallen on the ground having succumbed to death, O goddess, / the gaṇas were then dispatched to destroy the sacrifice. / Having gone there, those fierce gaṇas, by the hundreds and thousands, / misshapen, terrifying, frightful, bearing various weapons and of great strength, / released showers of arrows while making ferocious roars. / Then all the hosts of gods, the Vasus together with the suns, / the Viśvedevas and the Sādhyas, bows in hand, possessing great might, / marched forth to battle and unleashed sharp shafts. / Meeting there, the Pramathas fought with the gods; / they released showers of arrows like clouds discharging streams of water. / In their midst, a gaṇa of great might named Vīrabhadra / struck Śakra in the heart with a trident. / Rendered unconscious by that blow, he sank down. / Then the elephant Airāvata was struck on the frontal globes with a fist; / struck suddenly by him, that king of elephants, roaring with ferocious cries / and seized with fear, rushed towards the sacrificial enclosure. / In the meantime, the gods were routed by him; / then they sought refuge with Viṣṇu, the sole leader of the universe. / Then, filled with rage upon seeing the gods / all put to flight by the gaṇas, Viṣṇu quickly released the Sudarśana. / As that Sudarśana discus of Viṣṇu came hurtling with speed, / [Vīrabhadra] opened his mouth and suddenly swallowed it into his stomach. / When that unfailing discus, destroyer of the Daityas, was thus swallowed, / Nārāyaṇa, enraged, O goddess, rushed at Vīrabhadra. / Seizing him by both feet, he hurled him down to the ground from far away; / and as he was being struck on the ground with a mace, the Sudarśana, / accompanied by gouts of blood, issued forth from his mouth. / Having received a boon from me, O goddess, that best of gaṇas, Vīrabhadra, / did not succumb to death even though struck with the mace. / Then all the Pramathas, distressed by the power and might of Viṣṇu, / arrived with difficulty, suddenly, where I was staying, O goddess. / Seeing me with trident in hand, Viṣṇu vanished. / Indra too, together with the thirty [gods], with the ancestors and the brahmins, / his heart seized with terror of me, vanished from sight. / When the sacrifice had thus been destroyed and the host of gods was lost, / a gaṇa was then stationed by me at the gate of heaven, O goddess: / 'Entrance must never be granted to the thirty [gods], O lord of gaṇas! / A blockage of the gate must be vigilantly maintained by my command. / Whichever god is seen must undoubtedly be slain.' / And then heaven became deserted, and the gods were utterly defeated. / But when the gate of heaven was blocked, Śakra and the others, bewildered by fear, / consulted again and again and went to the world of Brahmā. / Before him, the entire blockage of heaven's gate was reported: / 'The gate of heaven is occupied by the gaṇas of the Great Lord, O grandfather! / Entrance has become difficult to obtain now that the gate is blocked. / By what means shall we go to the world of heaven as before? / We have no joy without heaven, O grandfather!' / Hearing these words of theirs, it was then spoken by Brahmā: / 'Lord Śaṃkara, the Great God, the master of the world, must be propitiated; / he, the maker of creation and destruction, is to be praised, revered, and saluted. / Difficult to attain is heaven, O gods, without his favor.

6.2.m:
He is the protector, the creator, the capable one, and he is our supreme refuge.
He alone is to be propitiated, and he is considered the most worthy of worship.
Therefore, with every effort, go to Śiva for refuge.
I shall explain the means; let it be heard attentively.
Accompanied by the thirty [gods], O Śakra, go quickly at my command
to the delightful Mahākālavana, to the east of Kapāleśvara.
The supreme liṅga Svargadvāra is situated there, O Vāsava,
fashioned by the Great God out of compassion for the worlds.
Propitiate it swiftly; he will grant your desire.'
Hearing the words of Brahmā, the thirty [gods] were exceedingly delighted.
They came then to the Mahākālavana, O great goddess,
and beheld the auspicious, supreme liṅga that bestows the gate of heaven.
By the mere sight of it, the gate of heaven opened.
All went to the world of heaven just as before, O glorious one.
Seeing the thirty [gods] free from fear, I was then petitioned by the gaṇas.
And they were all commanded by me: 'Turn back, O best of gaṇas!

6.2.m:
What was promised by myself—how could it turn out false?
The god who bestows the gate of heaven has undoubtedly been seen by the gods,
as spoken by Virañci in the delightful Mahākālavana.'
The hosts of the thirty [gods], beginning with Śakra, instantly reached the gate of heaven.
From then on, Śiva became renowned as Svargadvāreśvara.
He who bestows the world of heaven shall attain renown in the mortal world.
Those men in the world who behold Śiva as Svargadvāreśvara,
they indeed go to the world of heaven through the worship of Svargadvāreśvara.
Those who see the god Svargadvāreśvara even in passing
have no fear even in hundreds of millions of kalpas. (45)
Whatever merit is proclaimed to come from a thousand horse sacrifices,
greater than that is the merit, O goddess, from worshipping Svargadvāreśvara. (46)
Whatever sin has been accumulated previously through a thousand other births,
that sin dissolves through chanting the name of this liṅga. (47)

The glorious Mahādeva said:
Know the tenth, O Pārvatī, named Karkoṭeśvara, / by the mere sight of which one is not overcome by poisons. (1)
The serpents were cursed by their mother because they disobeyed her word: / 'Since my command was not obeyed by you in an act of sin, (2)
fire will burn you at the sacrifice of Janamejaya!' / Hearing then their mother's curse, terrified of death, the snakes (3)
all went to various places to preserve their lives, O illustrious one. / Śeṣa went to the snowy mountain to perform tapas, O beloved. (4)
The snake named Kambala went to the world of Brahmā; / then Śaṅkhacūḍa, lord of serpents, went to Maṇipūra; (5)
Kāliya, overwhelmed by fear, took refuge in the waters of the Yamunā. (6)
Thus those serpent kings, the nāgas, O lovely one of sweet smile, / all went to Kurukṣetra to perform tapas, O illustrious one. / Likewise the nāga Dhṛtarāṣṭra went to Prayāga, O beloved. (7)
And Elāpatra, lord of serpents, went to the world of Brahmā. / Having bowed to him who sat on the mother's lap, he spoke: (8)
'O god, we were cursed by our angry mother in your presence. / Why was she not prevented by you at the time of the curse?' (9)
Brahmā said:
'Your mother was not restrained by me because of the power of destined deeds; / indeed the snake sacrifice of King Janamejaya will take place. (10)
And you, child, by my command, go to the Mahākāla forest, / for the pacification of all serpents, quickly, filled with devotion. (11)
Worship the lord of gods near Mahāmāyā; / there your perfection will come to be by the grace of the god of gods.' (12)
Having gone there, Karkoṭa himself, collected in mind, O goddess, / worshipped the god, standing before Mahāmāyā. / Pleased with him, the lord of gods granted a boon, O illustrious one: (13)
'Those serpents that are cruel, sinful in conduct, and violent with poison, / their destruction will take place, but not of those who act righteously. (14)
I am pleased today with your devotion; enter into union with me.' / The nāga Karkoṭaka then dissolved into the god there, O beloved. (15)
From that time, the god Maheśvara became renowned as Karkoṭakeśvara; / by the mere sight of him, diseases perish. (16)
Whatever human being worships that god filled with devotion, / lordly power arises for him, and he redeems a hundred of his lineages. (17)
A sick person is freed from sickness, a suffering person is liberated from suffering; / by darśana alone, he immediately becomes freed from all sins. (18)
Those who regularly behold Karkoṭakeśvara / will obtain all desires and at the end dwell in my city. (19)
Those who see [him] on the fifth and on the fourteenth, or on a Sunday, / in their family snakes never cause harm. (20)
Even an unfortunate woman always attains good fortune; / a pregnant woman obtains a son free from disease, the ornament of his lineage; / afflictions caused by child-demons vanish, and there is no fear of untimely death. (21)
Whatever desire a devoted man meditates upon in his mind, / he attains that, however difficult to obtain, through the darśana of Karkoṭeśvara. (22)
This power that destroys sins has been told to you, O goddess, / of the god Karkoṭeśvara; hear now about the supreme Siddheśvara. (23)
Thus in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of eighty-one thousand [verses], in the fifth [section], the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorification of the eighty-four liṅgas, the tenth chapter, titled 'The Description of the Māhātmya of Karkoṭeśvara'. (10)
The glorious Mahādeva said:
Know the auspicious Siddheśvara to be the eleventh liṅga, O goddess,
situated near Vīrabhadra, the granter of all perfections. (1)
Long ago, in the Devadāru forest, brahmins endowed with yoga,
restrained, performed tapas in rivalry to obtain perfection. (2)
Some ate vegetables, some took no food, while others fed on leaves;
some used their teeth as a mortar, and others used stones to grind their food; (3)
some were devoted to the vīrāsana posture, others were engaged in inhaling smoke; (4)
some hung with feet upward and faces downward; some lived exposed to the open sky; (4)
others, composed in mind, performed the kṛcchra, cāndrāyaṇa, and other penances;
yet supreme perfection was not attained even in hundreds of years. (5)
Afflicted by distress, they reflected: 'How will perfection arise?
Perfection is not gained here even by difficult tapas! (6)

6.2.m: Austerity is not to be despised, nor righteousness; listen to the reason for this:
O you whose wealth is austerity, no accomplishment will come to you here;
for that austerity performed out of rivalry and desiring accomplishment was in vain.
From desire comes the loss of austerity, and from egotism comes pride;
and likewise from anger, greed, and delusion; of this there is no doubt.
He, however, who is free from rivalry, devoid of desire and anger,
and performs action with devotion, enjoys the fruit of austerity.
He who is perfumed with good impressions, single-minded, concentrated,
believing in the hereafter, and full of faith, enjoys the fruit of austerity.
The man who always regards another's wife as a mother,

If my word is to be carried out with an unwavering mind,

By them this earth was pervaded, together with its mountains and forests;
all their hermitages were wrecked, and sacrifices were ruined;

Hara said: / Know Kāmeśvara, O goddess, as the thirteenth liṅga there, / by the mere sight of which auspicious good fortune arises. / While Brahmā was meditating, desirous of progeny, O Pārvatī, / there arose a great mass of beauty, shaped with the splendour of the sun, / covered with ornaments, attractive, adorned with heavenly adornments. / Seeing him, supreme, divine, handsome, adorned with charm, / unfathomable and unknowable, Brahmā said to him then: / 'Who are you? For what purpose, or why have you come here? / Speak, you who resemble Manmatha! You appear to me like Kandarpa.' / Hearing Brahmā's words, he respectfully said to him: / 'I am a portion produced by your intention, as you desired creation. / O noble Prajāpati, what shall I do? Command me!'
Brahmā said:
'The Prajāpatis whom I created, desiring creation,
are unable to generate progeny, so that these [beings] might obtain happiness through desire.
You are the foremost leader in the creation of progeny; this universe depends on you.

Addressed thus by Brahmā, O goddess, Smara disappeared.
Angered, Brahmā cursed him: 'You shall certainly go to destruction
by the fire born of Bhava's eye, because you did not heed my word!'
Hearing that terrible curse, Kandarpa, agitated with fear,
bowed down to Brahmā and, bending low with folded hands, said:
'Be gracious, O Lord of the gods of gods, to me who have no other refuge!
The angers of masters do not attain complete intensity towards one who has taken refuge.'
Brahmā said:
'Since you possess matchless devotion toward me, O intelligent one,
therefore twelve abodes have been granted to you:
in the side-glances of passionate women, and indeed in their masses of hair,
in the hips, breasts, and navel, in the armpit, and in the lower lip,
in the spring, in the song of the cuckoo, in the moonlight, in the arrival of rain clouds.
And for the sake of desire, Madhu and Mādhava, with their armies, have been given by me.
Women are nectar-like and blessed, the essential cause in saṃsāra,

and the repositories of sexual pleasure, fashioned for the purpose of progeny.
By these excellent women the world has been subdued in this manner.
Where is the high-mindedness of a man whose mind is attached to women?
And how can there be self-mastery for one who has surrendered to respect for women?
Women alone were for the destruction of the former enemies of the immortals;
women alone are the sources of fear for the gods headed by Indra.
And for a man whose conduct is governed by women on every side,
humiliation and terrible helplessness arise.
For one whose mind is conquered by women, the emergence of calamity is easily obtained.'

And an effort was made against me, thinking again and again:
'God Śaṃkara is heard to be difficult to master in the three worlds;
who besides me is able to agitate that god?'
Having spoken thus, he approached the place where I remained in austerity,
accompanied by Rati with pride, supported by his friend Madhu.
Then Kāma saw me with a mass of matted hair, tawny and bound high,
sleepless for some purpose, adorned with the lord of serpents,
gazing straight ahead, with eyes directed at the tip of the bridge of my nose.
Then, having taken the form of a spider, relying on mere support,
Madana entered into my heart through the aperture of the hand.
Tormented by desire, you were remembered by me for the sake of union.
The divine contemplation of meditative absorption, perceiving its object directly,
and my purity vanished at that very instant, O Pārvatī.
I became maddened, indeed, with an agitation caused by Madana.
Taking hold of steadfastness with effort, O goddess, it was rejected by me.

Manmatha, the producer of harmful things, was seen by me within my heart:
'I shall burn him residing in my body through the practice of sense-withdrawal!'
He would enter a non-human womb if he enters a yogin.
Fixing [the mind] upon the external fire, one should burn away that which resides in the body. // 31
Meanwhile, Madana too, burning intensely,
taking a body at will, difficult to perceive, and consisting of destructive passion, came forth. // 32
Standing then at the foot of a mango tree, the friend of Spring,
Makaradhvaja, discharged the arrow named Mohana. // 33
And that arrow effortlessly struck my heart.
Then, O goddess, I grew enraged and manifested my third eye. // 34
By a spark from that eye, as the dwellers of heaven cried out,
Kandarpa, the pride of lovers, was instantly reduced to ashes. // 35

Why do you leave me, O lord, who am faithful to my husband and whose very life is her husband?” // 37
As she was thus weeping, a bodiless voice said to her:
“Do not weep, O large-eyed one! This husband of yours
shall rise again by the grace of Śiva, the god of gods.” // 38
Then, O goddess, at that moment I was prayed to, O beloved:
“O Supreme Lord, this Kāma was burned by you in anger, // 39
through whose absence, O lord, creation on the face of the earth has truly been destroyed.
Show mercy, O Lord of gods! Give my husband back to me, a wretched woman!” // 40
Then I spoke, O goddess, to that Rati who was speaking piteously:
“Today, by this Madana, my mind was agitated; // 41
therefore his body was burned by me. I shall revive him by your favor.

therefore he will wander among creatures as bodiless (Anaṅga).

6.2.m:
Having gone there, even without a body, endowed with devotion,
he beheld the supreme liṅga that bestows the desired fruits. // 45
The liṅga, being pleased, said: “O Kāma, you shall obtain your desire;
though bodiless, you will become powerful, without a doubt. // 46
You shall take birth in the womb of Rukmiṇī from union with Kṛṣṇa,
and will be renowned in the world by the name of the slayer of Śambara. // 47
Because I have been pleased in mind by you, though bodiless,
therefore, O Kāma, I shall always be celebrated by your name. // 48
Those who behold you, Kandarpa, filled with supreme devotion,
shall eternally attain the destination that bestows everlasting bliss. // 49
They shall have long life, they shall have beauty,
and their lineage shall be immaculate—those who behold you, O Manmatha. // 50
Sovereignty, supreme enjoyments, women endowed with divine arts,
and free from disease shall be their progeny, without a doubt. // 51
Those men who behold me with devotion on the thirteenth day of the bright half of Caitra,

6.2.m:
The glorious Viśvanātha said:
Know the twenty-second [liṅga] to be named Karkaṭeśvara, / by the mere darśana of which an animal womb is not seen [again]. // 1
Formerly, in the Bṛhatkalpa, there was a king who was the embodiment of righteousness, / a friend of Śakra, by whom daityas were slain by the thousands; // 2
by whose splendor the moon, the sun, and others were rendered lustreless, / and by whom the subjects were protected after slaying his foes in battle; // 3
who could assume forms at will and was undefeated in battles. / His wife, named Bhānumatī, was the beauty of the three worlds, // 4
the chief queen of that king, dearer even than life, / who shone among ten thousand women like Lakṣmī herself. // 5
The king was never left alone by thousands of kings. / Once, having gone to a solitary place, with a mind filled with wonder, // he asked his family priest, the best of ṛṣis, Vaśiṣṭha: // 6
'O venerable one, by what righteous deed is my peerless fortune [obtained]? / And why is this immense, unbearable splendor of mine seen?' // 7
Vaśiṣṭha said:
'Formerly, O king, you were born into the śūdra caste, / accompanied by many faults, with this wicked wife. // 8
Living for very many years with a wicked heart, / your self overcome with great anger, always speaking harshly, // 9
you always stole the property of brahmins, always reviled the Vedas, / were always envious, O king, and always betrayed trust. // 10
Then, having met your death, in due course you arrived in hell. / You were exceedingly roasted on a copper frying-pan for fifteen years, // 11
in Raurava, Kumbhīpāka, and that known as Mahāraurava. / Having been made into numerous tiny fragments the size of sesame seeds, // 12
you were placed in a crucible, O king, and torn apart on the sword-leaved trees. / For the purification of the remainder of your sins, you were made to descend to earth, // 13
having been given the form of a crab by Yama, O earth-ruler. / There is the famed lake of Śiva in the supreme Mahākālavana; // 14
whatever is given, muttered, done, offered in sacrifice, worship of gods and the like, / all that action in that lake is renowned as imperishable. // 15
You were thrown there then by virtue of that future meritorious act. / There you remained, O protector of the earth, for a period of five years. // 16
Once, you went slowly upon the ground of the bank to play. / Seeing you there, a crow seized you in the hollow of its beak, // 17
and flew up into the pathway of the sky; it was struck severely by you. / Then, struck and pained by your feet with sharp strikes, // 18
you were dropped from the hollow of its beak by the agitated crow. / To the east of the gate of heaven, in the very meritorious abode of the Goddess, // 19
you were cast down quickly [into the sanctuary] of Śiva, tormented by the thrusts of the beak; / you died right there in the presence of the supreme deity. // 20
As soon as that worn-out, former crab-body was abandoned, / in that very moment, [endowed with] a divine body and adorned with celestial ornaments, // 21
becoming a lord of the Vidyādharas through the māhātmya of that liṅga, / in an aerial chariot that moved at will, being honored by the lords of gaṇas, // 22
as you were going to heaven, you were asked respectfully by hosts of gods: / "Who is this noble being going joyfully along the celestial path from the sky?" // 23
Then, everything was told formerly to the gods by the gaṇas of Rudra, / the entire event in detail, the deliverance from the state of a crab: // 24
"O lords of gods, this power belongs to that liṅga!" / And it was immediately spoken by the gods: "Through the power of this liṅga, // 25
since one released from the womb of a crab has attained the bliss of heaven, / therefore he shall be known in the world by the name Karkaṭeśvara." // 26
From that time forward, this deity is known as Karkaṭeśvara. / By you, O king, great pleasures were enjoyed in heaven at your pleasure. // 27
You have come back to earth again, and an undisputed kingdom has been obtained. / All this has now occurred for you through the māhātmya of that liṅga. // 28
Therefore, O earth-ruler, quickly worship that liṅga again.' / Then, having attained recollection of his previous births through the words of Vaśiṣṭha, // 29
his own past deed was remembered by that ruler of the earth. / Having gone again, he worshipped that liṅga with great effort. // 30
He attained absorption into that liṅga with his very body, O Pārvatī. / Those who always worship [the liṅga] named Karkaṭeśvara with devotion, / having enjoyed pleasures on earth for a long time, go to the supreme state. // 31
Those who behold the god Karkaṭeśvara according to rule / on the eighth or fourteenth [day]—listen to the meritorious fruit for them! // 32
In aerial chariots brilliant like the radiance of the sun that fulfill all desires, / when they die, they go to my city together with twenty-one generations of their family. // 33

6.2.m:
There, served by thousands of charming women with celestial, great enjoyments, / they indeed dwell for hundreds of millions of kalpas, O goddess.
At the end of that, they remain for the same amount of time in Viṣṇu's abode, / served by thousands of women with diverse Vaiṣṇava enjoyments.
Having reached the world of Brahmā from the world of Viṣṇu, joyful once more, / and having enjoyed manifold pleasures, they go from there to the supreme abode.
Whatever merit is attained by ten horse sacrifices, that is the fruit attained by a pilgrimage / to the god Karkaṭeśvara. Hear now of Meghanādeśvara.
Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, entitled 'The Description of the Māhātmya of Karkaṭeśvara' in the Māhātmya of the Eighty-Four Liṅgas in the Avantī Khaṇḍa, the fifth [section] of the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

6.2.m: At the junction between Kali and Dvāpara, due to his sin, O spirited lady,
A terrible drought occurred in the world lasting twelve years. // 5
The thousand-eyed one did not rain; the lord became adverse.
Even at night's end, varieties of clouds were not to be seen at all, let alone elsewhere. // 6
Rivers had their floods of water diminished, and some disappeared altogether then.
Sacrifices and Vedic recitation ceased; auspicious utterances of vaṣaṭ were gone. // 7
Agriculture and cattle-rearing were ruined; markets also shut down.
The lands were strewn with skeletons and bones, crowded with wailing people. // 8
Cities were mostly deserted; settlements of villages were burned down.
Bereft of cattle, goats, horses, and buffaloes, people were devouring one another. // 9
Having abandoned their hermitages, they ran about hither and thither.
Overwhelmed with sorrow, the brahmins died or perished, O Pārvatī. // 10
The entire creation was uprooted, both all the moving and the unmoving.
In the meantime, the gods headed by Śakra, agitated with fear, // 11
Sought refuge with Janārdana, the god of gods, who gives refuge,
On the northern shore of the milk ocean, at charming Śvetadvīpa, // 12
Auspicious, whose virtues were beyond compare even with the worlds of Brahmā and others,
Ever bestowing joy, tranquil, radiant like ten million suns, // 13
Where palaces, couches, and seats were arranged according to desire,
Illuminated by diamonds, sapphires, lapis lazuli, moonstones, and other gems, // 14
Free from all diseases accompanied by the fear of old age and death.

"O God, the entire world is ruined, afflicted by drought;

roaring through the vault of heaven, arose from the middle of the liṅga;

‘You shall be invincible to all the rulers of the earth;
you will be the destroyer of all before long, O descendant of Bhṛgu. 6
Take this stout axe, my son, produced from the flames of fire;

6.2.s: anena śitaśastreṇa tataḥ khyāto bhavi ṣyati .. 7 ..
6.2.d: अनेन शितशस्त्रेण ततः ख्यातो भवि ष्यति .. 7 ..
6.2.m: by this sharp weapon you shall henceforth be famous.’ 7
Then, after some time, King Kārttavīryārjuna,
born in the lineage of the Haihayas and renowned as the Thousand-Armed, 8
evil-minded, struck down Jamadagni for the sake of the wish-granting cow.
Seeing his father slain, Rāma, enraged, said this: 9

6.2.s: atha paśyaṃtu me vīryaṃ trayo lokāḥ sanātanam ..
6.2.d: अथ पश्यंतु मे वीर्यं त्रयो लोकाः सनातनम् ..
6.2.m: ‘Now let the three worlds behold my eternal valor,
and let that evil-minded killer of a brahmin, the son of Kṛtavīrya, behold it, 10
by whom my father, who was always devoted to good deeds, was slain!

6.2.s: tasya bāhusahasraṃ tu chetsyāmīha na saṃśayaḥ .. 11 ..
6.2.d: तस्य बाहुसहस्रं तु छेत्स्यामीह न संशयः .. 11 ..
6.2.m: I shall sever his thousand arms here—of this there is no doubt!’ 11
Having spoken thus, his eyes red with rage, [he seized] Kārttavīryārjuna upon the earth
and having overpowered him at will as he cried out again and again, // 12
the descendant of Bhṛgu cut off his entire thousand arms
with a sharp battle-axe, along with his kinsmen then. // 13
He threw him down from his chariot and slew the king, O dear one;
thrice seven times the earth was cleared of kṣatriyas by him. // 14

6.2.s: kṛtvā niḥkṣatriyāṃ caiva bhārgavaḥ sa mahābalaḥ ..
6.2.d: कृत्वा निःक्षत्रियां चैव भार्गवः स महाबलः ..
6.2.m: Having made the earth devoid of kṣatriyas, that mighty Bhārgava,
for the destruction of all sins, performed a horse sacrifice. // 15
In that sacrifice of vast gift-giving, as the priestly fee, the descendant of Bhṛgu
joyfully gave the earth to Kaśyapa, the son of Marīci; // 16
and white horses born of Varuṇa, and a chariot, the best of chariot-warriors,
imperishable gold, milch cows, and lordly elephants, the great-minded one [gave]. // 17
Then, in that great sacrifice, the horse sacrifice, he of great renown [offered all this];
yet still the guilt of slaughter arising from many living beings did not depart. // 18
“Thus indeed, in the Purāṇas and in all varieties of traditional scriptures,
an expiation for killers of the trusting is heard of: // 19
By the horse sacrifice, the sin of killing a brahmin is destroyed,
or by a twelve-year vow, if a single one was committed on earth. // 20
Yet by me, cruel as I am, countless living beings were killed:
the trusting, the heedless, and those still in the womb, again and again; // 21

6.2.s: striyo vṛddhāśca bālāśca mātā caiva viśeṣataḥ ..
6.2.d: स्त्रियो वृद्धाश्च बालाश्च माता चैव विशेषतः ..
6.2.m: women, the aged, children, and especially my own mother.”

6.2.s: iti duḥkhānvito rāmo viṣādaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ .. 22 ..
6.2.d: इति दुःखान्वितो रामो विषादं परमं गतः .. 22 ..
6.2.m: Filled with sorrow in this way, Rāma sank into the deepest despondency. // 22

6.2.s: ciṃtayitvā muhūrtaṃ tu gato raivatakaṃ girim ..
6.2.d: चिंतयित्वा मुहूर्तं तु गतो रैवतकं गिरिम् ..
6.2.m: Reflecting for a moment, he went to Mount Raivataka,
and there he performed terrible austerity for many host of years, O dear one. // 23
Yet still the guilt of slaughter arising from many living beings did not depart.

6.2.s: atha rāmo jagāmātha mahendre malaye tathā .. 24 ..
6.2.d: अथ रामो जगामाथ महेन्द्रे मलये तथा .. 24 ..
6.2.m: Then Rāma went next to Mahendra and to Malaya, // 24
to Sahya, to the lovely Himālaya, and to the holy hermitage of Badarī.
Having roamed across all the mountains, he went to the Narmadā for ritual ablution, // 25
and to the Yamunā, the Candrabhāgā, the Gaṅgā that flows through three paths,

6.2.s: irāvatīṃ vitastāṃ ca parāṃ carmaṇvatīṃ śubhām .. 26 ..
6.2.d: इरावतीं वितस्तां च परां चर्मण्वतीं शुभाम् .. 26 ..
6.2.m: the Irāvatī, the Vitastā, the supreme and auspicious Carmaṇvatī, // 26

6.2.s: viśālāṃ kapilāṃ durgāṃ gaṃbhīrāṃ gomatīṃ śivām ..
6.2.d: विशालां कपिलां दुर्गां गंभीरां गोमतीं शिवाम् ..
6.2.m: the Viśālā, the Kapilā, the Durgā, the Gambhīrā, the auspicious Gomatī,

6.2.s: godāvarīṃ daśārṇāṃ ca puṇyāṃ bhīmarathīṃ tathā .. 27 ..
6.2.d: गोदावरीं दशार्णां च पुण्यां भीमरथीं तथा .. 27 ..
6.2.m: the Godāvarī, the Daśārṇā, and the holy Bhīmarathī; // 27

6.2.s: gayāṃ caiva kurukṣetraṃ naimiṣaṃ puṣkaraṃ tathā ..
6.2.d: गयां चैव कुरुक्षेत्रं नैमिषं पुष्करं तथा ..
6.2.m: and to Gayā, Kurukṣetra, Naimiṣa, and Puṣkara,
Aṭṭahāsa, Prabhāsa, Kedāra, and Amareśvara. // 28
Though his pilgrimage was completed, the Bhārgava, tormented with sorrow, thought:

6.2.s: na nūnaṃ tīrthamāhātmyaṃ dṛśyate bhuvi sāṃpratam .. 29 ..
6.2.d: न नूनं तीर्थमाहात्म्यं दृश्यते भुवि सांप्रतम् .. 29 ..
6.2.m: “Surely the majesty of sacred fords is no longer seen on earth today! // 29

6.2.s: na gatā brahmahatyā me kṛto dharmo nirarthakaḥ ..
6.2.d: न गता ब्रह्महत्या मे कृतो धर्मो निरर्थकः ..
6.2.m: The sin of killing a brahmin has not left me; the religious merit I performed is useless!
Falsely is it stated in the scriptures that through auspicious sacred fords, gifts, and the like [sins are removed];

6.2.s: yadi syātsatyametacca naṣṭaṃ jātaṃ kathaṃ mama .. 5.2.29.30 ..
6.2.d: यदि स्यात्सत्यमेतच्च नष्टं जातं कथं मम .. 5.2.29.30 ..
6.2.m: if this were true, how has [no sin] of mine been destroyed?” // 30
At that very time, Nārada, the best of sages,
came to that region where Rāma was dwelling. // 31
Dejected in countenance, miserable, deliberating again and again—
having seen [Nārada], Rāma in such a state then addressed Nārada: // 32

6.2.s: bhobho nārada devarṣe śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ ..
6.2.d: भोभो नारद देवर्षे शृणु मे परमं वचः ..
6.2.m: “O Nārada, divine seer, hear my momentous speech!
My mother was slain long ago at my father’s command, O best of the twice-born; // 33
because of the insult to my father, kings were slain by me on earth;

6.2.s: garbhā vidāritāḥ strīṇāṃ bālā vṛddhāśca yoṣitaḥ.. 34 ..
6.2.d: गर्भा विदारिताः स्त्रीणां बाला वृद्धाश्च योषितः.. 34 ..
6.2.m: the wombs of women were torn open, and children, the old, and women [were killed]. // 34
Incessantly people were slaughtered by me, sorrowless and pitiless.
Afterward, disgust arose in me as I looked toward the other world. // 35
The horse sacrifice was performed, and gifts of many kinds were given;
I bathed in all sacred fords and in all mountain torrents; // 36
austerity was endured on mountains, offerings were poured, and prayers continuously recited.

6.2.s: brahmahatyāvināśārthaṃṃ kiṃ kiṃ nātra mayā kṛtam ..37..
6.2.d: ब्रह्महत्याविनाशार्थंं किं किं नात्र मया कृतम् ..37..
6.2.m: For the destruction of the sin of killing a brahmin, what, indeed, was not done by me here? // 37

6.2.s: paraṃ naiva gatā hatyā tasmātsarvaṃ nirarthakam .. 38 ..
6.2.d: परं नैव गता हत्या तस्मात्सर्वं निरर्थकम् .. 38 ..
6.2.m: Yet the guilt of slaughter has not at all departed; therefore, everything is useless!” // 38

6.2.s: iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā nārado bhagavānṛṣiḥ ..
6.2.d: इति तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा नारदो भगवानृषिः ..
6.2.m: Having heard his words, the venerable seer Nārada,

6.2.s: pratyuvāca hitaṃ satyaṃ ciraṃ dhyātvā vacastadā ..
6.2.d: प्रत्युवाच हितं सत्यं चिरं ध्यात्वा वचस्तदा ..
6.2.m: having meditated for a long time, then spoke beneficial and truthful words in reply:

6.2.s: bhobho rāma kimātmānaṃ na smarasyadhunā harim .. 39 ..
6.2.d: भोभो राम किमात्मानं न स्मरस्यधुना हरिम् .. 39 ..
6.2.m: “O Rāma, why do you not remember yourself now as Hari? // 39
By you yourself was previously described the destroyer of the sin of killing a brahmin
in the sacred field of Mahākālavana, the foremost and supreme among sacred fields.
In that sacred field is the great liṅga that destroys the sin of killing a brahmin.” // 40
O fortunate one, there is Jaṭeśvara, which grants all perfections.
O Rāma, who have taken descent, go there without delay!”
Having heard Nārada’s words and remembering that unsurpassed sacred field,
he went quickly, O goddess, to the Mahākālavana.
He worshiped the liṅga, and then the [sin of] murder was destroyed.
Then, O goddess, being pleased, I emerged from the middle of the liṅga.
The son of Jamadagni was told by me: “I shall grant whatever desire you cherish.”
Then that Rāma, bowing his neck in devotion, said:
“May I always have abundant devotion to your lotus feet!
Grant this boon today, O Maheśvara, if you are pleased.”

6.2.s: ityukto'haṃ tadā tena yathā tuṣṭena pārvati ..
6.2.d: इत्युक्तोऽहं तदा तेन यथा तुष्टेन पार्वति ..
6.2.m: Having been spoken to thus by him then, as I was pleased, O Pārvatī,

6.2.s: tasmai dattā mayābhīṣṭā varā kīrttikarā sthitiḥ .. 45 ..
6.2.d: तस्मै दत्ता मयाभीष्टा वरा कीर्त्तिकरा स्थितिः .. 45 ..
6.2.m: I granted him his desired boons and a state that brings renown:

6.2.s: adyaprabhṛti te nāmnā devaḥ khyāto bhaviṣyati ..
6.2.d: अद्यप्रभृति ते नाम्ना देवः ख्यातो भविष्यति ..
6.2.m: “From this day forward, the god will be renowned by your name.”

6.2.s: tadā rāmeśvara iti triṣu lokeṣu gīyate .. 46 ..
6.2.d: तदा रामेश्वर इति त्रिषु लोकेषु गीयते .. 46 ..
6.2.m: Then it was sung in the three worlds as Rāmeśvara.

6.2.s: bhaktyā ye pūjayiṣyaṃti devaṃ rāmeśvaraṃ param ..
6.2.d: भक्त्या ये पूजयिष्यंति देवं रामेश्वरं परम् ..
6.2.m: Those who worship the supreme god Rāmeśvara with devotion,
their sins accumulated since birth perish that very moment.

6.2.s: sa eva puṇyavānpūjya iha loke paratra ca ..
6.2.d: स एव पुण्यवान्पूज्य इह लोके परत्र च ..
6.2.m: He indeed is meritorious and venerable in this world and the next,

6.2.s: yaḥ paśyati naro bhaktyā devaṃ rāmeśvaraṃ śivam .. 48 ..
6.2.d: यः पश्यति नरो भक्त्या देवं रामेश्वरं शिवम् .. 48 ..
6.2.m: the person who beholds the auspicious god Rāmeśvara with devotion.
Those who rejoice at the darśana and the worship of the god,
they too, released from sins, go to my abode.
And whatever terrible sin, even a thousand brahmin-murders,
that sin dissolves through the worship of Rāmeśvara.
Whatever fruit is difficult to obtain by brahmins even through sacrifices like the Vājapeya,
that is obtained with ease merely from the darśana of glorious Rāmeśvara.
Heroes who are slain facing [the foe] on the battlefield for cows and brahmins—
a destination far higher than theirs belongs to one who sees the auspicious Rāmeśvara.
The worlds are always conquered by him, just as the three worlds were conquered by Rāma,

6.2.s: dṛṣṭaṃ yena sadā bhaktyā liṃgaṃ rāmeśvaraṃ śivam .. 53 ..
6.2.d: दृष्टं येन सदा भक्त्या लिंगं रामेश्वरं शिवम् .. 53 ..
6.2.m: by whom the auspicious liṅga of Rāmeśvara is constantly seen with devotion.

6.2.s: eṣa te kathito devi prabhāvaḥ pāpanāśanaḥ ..
6.2.d: एष ते कथितो देवि प्रभावः पापनाशनः ..
6.2.m: This power that destroys sin has been told to you, O goddess,
concerning the god Rāmeśvara. Now listen about Cyavaneśvara.

6.2.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvaṃtya khaṇḍe caturaśītiliṃgamāhātmye rāmeśvaramāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmaikonatriṃśodhyāyaḥ.. 29..
6.2.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवंत्य खण्डे चतुरशीतिलिंगमाहात्म्ये रामेश्वरमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामैकोनत्रिंशोध्यायः.. 29..
6.2.m: Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter, entitled “Description of the Māhātmya of Rāmeśvara,” in the Māhātmya of the Eighty-Four Liṅgas in the fifth Avantī section of the glorious Skandapurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand verses.

śrīviśvanātha uvāca..

6.2.d:
श्रीविश्वनाथ उवाच..
त्रिंशत्तमं विजानीहि त्वं देवि च्यवनेश्वरम्..
यस्य दर्शनमात्रेण स्वर्गभ्रंशो न जायते..1..
भृगोर्महर्षेः पुत्रश्च च्यवनो नाम पार्वति..
स्थाणुभूतस्तपस्तेपे निराहारो महामुनिः .. 2 ..
वितस्तायास्तटे रम्ये बहुवर्षगणान्किल ..
सवल्मीकोऽभवद्विप्रो लताभिरभिसंवृतः .. 3 ..
कालेन महता देवि समाकीर्णः पिपीलकैः ..
तथा स संवृतो धीमान्मृत्पिंड इव सर्वशः .. 4 ..
आजगाम तमुद्देशं विहर्तुं वन उत्तमे ..
शर्यातिर्नाम धर्मात्मा सकुटुंबो मुदान्वितः .. 5 ..
तस्य स्त्रीणां सहस्राणि चत्वार्यासन्परिग्रहः ..
एकैव तु सुता सुभ्रूः सुकन्यानाम नामतः .. 6 ..
सा सखीभिः परिवृता सर्वाभरणभूषिता ..
सा भ्रम्यमाणा वल्मीके दृष्ट्वा भार्गवचक्षुषी .. 7 ..
सा कौतुकात्कण्टकेन बुद्धिमोहवती तदा ..
किं नु खल्विदमित्युक्त्वा निर्बिभेदास्य लोचने .. 8 ..
अभवत्स तया विद्धो नेत्रयोः परमार्तिमान् ..

6.2.m:
Śrī Viśvanātha said:
Know the thirtieth [liṅga], O goddess, to be Cyavaneśvara, / by the mere sight of which one does not fall from heaven. (1)
O Pārvatī, the son of the great seer Bhṛgu, named Cyavana, / that great sage, becoming motionless like a pillar, performed austerity without food (2)
on the delightful bank of the Vitastā for many series of years indeed. / That brahmin became an anthill, covered around with creepers. (3)
Over a great span of time, O goddess, crowded with ants, / the wise one was thus enclosed on all sides like a lump of clay. (4)
To that region, to sport in the excellent forest, / came the righteous Śaryāti, joyful, accompanied by his family. (5)
He had four thousand women as his wives; / but he had only one daughter of beautiful brows, named Sukanyā. (6)
Surrounded by her friends and adorned with all ornaments, / wandering about, she saw the two eyes of the descendant of Bhṛgu in the anthill. (7)
Then out of curiosity, with a mind bewildered, with a thorn, / saying, “What indeed is this?”, she pierced his two eyes. (8)
Pierced by her in both eyes, he suffered supreme pain; / then he obstructed the feces and urine of Śaryāti’s army. (9)
Then, with feces and urine obstructed, the king was tormented; / enraged, the king then spoke in a faltering voice: (10)
“Who here today has done harm to the great-souled descendant of Bhṛgu, / who is constant in austerity, aged, and especially wrathful? (11)
Whether it was done wittingly or unwittingly, speak of it without delay!” / All the soldiers said to him: “We do not know of any harm.” (12)
Then the protector of the earth, both gently and sternly, / deeply sorrowful, repeatedly questioned his own people himself. (13)
Seeing her father distressed, Sukanyā then said to him: / “I saw a certain being in the anthill possessing great radiance. (14)
It was perceived like a firefly, and that was pierced by me at close quarters.” / Hearing this, Śaryāti went swiftly to the anthill. (15)
There he saw the descendant of Bhṛgu, advanced in austerity and advanced in age; / with folded hands, that ruler of the earth made an appeal for the sake of his army: (16)
“Whatever harm was done to you by the young girl out of ignorance, O earthly god, / this very maiden of exceedingly firm vows I give to you. (17)
Take her as your wife; be gracious, O best of the twice-born!” / Thereupon the Bhārgava Cyavana said to the ruler of the earth: (18)
“If it is so, having received her, I shall forgive, O ruler of the earth.” / The ruler of the earth gave his daughter to that Cyavana. (19)
And having accepted that maiden, the venerable one became propitiated; / once the grace was obtained, the king with his army went to his realm. (20)
Having obtained the ascetic as her husband, the irreproachable Sukanyā / always served him with affection, austerity, and discipline. (21)
Then, after some time, O beloved, the two Nāsatyas, the Aśvins, / saw that Sukanyā who had bathed and was uncovered. (22)
Seeing her with charming limbs, like the daughter of the king of the gods, / running up, they both said: “Whose [wife] are you, O most beautiful one?” (23)
That highly fortunate one, devoted to her husband, said: / “The daughter of Śaryāti and indeed the wife of Cyavana.” (24)
Then the two Aśvins, laughing, said to her yet again: / “Why, being such as you are, to a husband shattered by old age (25)
[are you devoted], abandoning him here, O auspicious one, excluded from the pleasures of desire? / Leaving the old Cyavana, choose one of us two! (26)
For a husband, O girl resembling an offspring of the gods, do not waste your youth!” / Addressed thus, Sukanyā said to those two Dasras: (27)
“I am devoted to the godlike Cyavana; do not doubt me in this way!” / Then they both said to her again: “We two are the best physicians of the gods. (28)
We shall make your husband young and endowed with beauty; / on this condition, summon us, O slender-waisted one!” (29)

“Since I, being old, have been made endowed with beauty

Hearing that, with joyful minds, the two gods went to heaven.
He caused the two Aśvins, the Nāsatyas, to sacrifice as worthy of Soma. (39)
[Indra said:] “The two physicians of the deities are condemned on account of that occupation.

whose servant is Śakra, whose obedient followers are the gods,
who is capable, the protector of the universe, the cause of creation and destruction.” (42)
Having said this, O goddess, Cyavana went to the forest of Mahākāla.

As [Indra] was striking him, the descendant of Bhṛgu paralysed his arm.
Through the power of this liṅga, pleased by his veneration,
at that moment a flame burst forth from the middle of the liṅga.
Scorched by it and bewildered in mind, all the hosts of gods,

Hearing the words of the gods, afflicted with fear,

Because it was worshipped by the great-souled Cyavana, O goddess,
this [liṅga] became renowned throughout the three worlds as Cyavaneśvara.
Those devotees who shall worship the lord of gods, Cyavaneśvara,
their sin originating from birth is destroyed at that very instant.
The man who constantly beholds the one named Cyavaneśvara
freed from the sorrow of birth, old age, and diseases, shall attain liberation.
Whatever desire a man may mentally contemplate as dear,
he attains that very thing, difficult to obtain, from the darśana of Cyavaneśvara.
Those who behold the god Cyavaneśvara according to observance,
leaving their body behind, O beloved, go to my realm.
Whoever hears this auspicious, sacred story that removes all sins,
that meritorious soul goes to the supreme divine abode, without a doubt.
Even one destitute of devotion and lacking rites who beholds it incidentally,
he attains an auspicious destiny accessible only to yogins, O renowned lady.

6.2.m: “By what wicked sinner was this vile deed done, that my father,

He burned his father on the fire, quickly took water,

“Since he has slain my father, a learned man devoted to his own duty,

Meanwhile, the king was afflicted with leprosy;

On the delightful bank of the Śiprā, to the east of Keśavārka,

6.2.s: tatra tvaṃ gaccha rājeṃdra kāṃtyā yukto bhaviṣyasi .. 27 ..
6.2.d: तत्र त्वं गच्छ राजेंद्र कांत्या युक्तो भविष्यसि .. 27 ..

6.2.m: Those who worship the supreme Lumpeśvara liṅga with devotion,

Śrī Hara said:
Hear now of the forty-second deity, Gaṅgeśvara,
by the mere darśana of whom one obtains the fruit of all sacred fords.
From the foot of Nārāyaṇa, the origin of the universe and support of the pole star, (1)

6.2.s: padātpravṛttā yā devī gaṃgā tripathagā nadī ..

6.2.m: the goddess, the river Gaṅgā who flows along three paths, issued forth from that foot.

and then purified by contact with the rising rays of the sun,

6.2.m: she fell upon the summit of Meru, and from there she went in four directions. (3)

6.2.s: tatra sīteti vikhyātā yayau caitrarathaṃ vanam .. 5 ..

6.2.m: the Ocean, lord of rivers, delighted in her company. (14)

and the Ocean too went to the eternal world of Brahmā,

Then Gaṅgā, the best of rivers, approached the Grandfather [Brahmā].

but the royal seer Mahābhiṣa looked upon the river without hesitation. (17)

6.2.s: tasya bhāvaṃ viditvā'tha brahmaṇā sa tiraskṛtaḥ ..

6.2.m: Knowing his intention, Brahmā rebuked him,
and he was told: 'Born among mortals, you shall attain these worlds again.' (18)

6.2.m: Hearing that terrible curse, Gaṅgā spoke these words: (20)

6.2.m: Then Brahmā answered that river, the purifier of the worlds: (22)

In the delightful forest of Mahākāla, frequented by Siddhas and Gandharvas,
on the southern bank of the Śiprā, there is an excellent liṅga, (24)
which brings all perfections, holy, and the destroyer of all sins.

6.2.m: Worship it with diligence; it will grant your desire.' (25)

6.2.m: 'Going there is desirable to me, since my friend is there;
the Śiprā also is dear to me, holy and destroying great sins.' (26)

6.2.d: इति संचिंत्य मनसा दिव्या देवनदी तदा ..
6.2.m: Reflecting thus in her mind, the divine river of the gods then

She then worshipped [it] with milk according to the divine rite.

6.2.d: दृष्ट्वा शिप्रां सखीं तत्र संश्लेषं चाभवत्तयोः .. 28 ..

6.2.m: From then on, that Śiprā became eastward-flowing.

6.2.m: Having spoken thus, Gaṅgā departed, remaining there with a portion [of herself].

6.2.m: Whoever beholds Gaṅgeśvara after bathing in the waters of Śiprā, O beloved,

Whoever, composed in mind, beholds the god Gaṅgeśvara

6.2.m: This power that destroys sins has been told to you, O goddess,
concerning the god Gaṅgeśvara; now listen to the supreme [power] of Aṅgāreśvara. // 41

Know the forty-third, O daughter of the mountain,
by merely seeing which all prosperities arise. // 1
Long ago, in the first kalpa, one with a crooked body and reddish hue,

have been blocked by the exceedingly fierce, cruel planets, O grandfather!”
Hearing the words of the gods, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds,
"O gods, I am afraid of those exceedingly powerful planets. .. 31 ..
I know all the power of the cruel-minded planets.
You were constantly tormented by Saturn when retrograde; .. 32 ..
Varuṇa, the lord of aquatic creatures, was sorely afflicted by Mars;
and Indra was repeatedly cast down from his kingdom by Ketu. .. 33 ..

6.2.s: śiraśchedo mayā prāpto vakreṇa raviṇā purā ..
6.2.d: शिरश्छेदो मया प्राप्तो वक्रेण रविणा पुरा ..
6.2.m: Formerly, my own head was severed on account of a retrograde Sun.
Individually they are so powerful; how much more so when gathered together?
Therefore let us all go to Mahādeva for refuge." .. 34 ..

6.2.m: I was addressed by all the gods: "Protect us who have sought refuge!

6.2.m: You are our creator, ordainer, and the cause of creation and dissolution. .. 36 ..
O Mahādeva, the clouds have been blocked on all sides by the cruel planets;
they bring no rain, O Lord. A terrible drought,
lasting a hundred years, has arisen to destroy all living beings."

6.2.m: Having heard their words, O fair-faced one, I understood,

6.2.d: क्रूरग्रहाणां सामर्थ्यं यथा च विदितं मम..38..
6.2.m: knowing well the power of the cruel planets. .. 38 ..
Knowing this, O great goddess, an expedient was devised by me.

6.2.s: uttaro nāma yo megho meghaiḥ koṭibhirāvṛtaḥ..
6.2.d: उत्तरो नाम यो मेघो मेघैः कोटिभिरावृतः..
6.2.m: The cloud named Uttara, surrounded by tens of millions of clouds,
was summoned, arrived at that very moment, and said: "What shall I do?" .. 39 ..
He was told by me: "By my command, go accompanied by the dense clouds
to the charming Mahākālavana, which grants the fruits of desired ends. .. 40 ..
To the south of the god Gaṅgeśvara is an excellent liṅga.

6.2.s: tamārādhaya yatnena sa te dāsyati vāṃchitam .. 41 ..
6.2.d: तमाराधय यत्नेन स ते दास्यति वांछितम् .. 41 ..
6.2.m: Worship it with diligence; it will grant your desire." .. 41 ..
Having been thus addressed by me, the cloud Uttara, accompanied by the clouds,
went in haste to the supreme Mahākālavana. .. 42 ..
Beholding the rain-making liṅga, he worshipped it with devotion.

6.2.s: śiprājalaṃ gṛhītvā tu snātvā snātvā prayatnataḥ ..
6.2.d: शिप्राजलं गृहीत्वा तु स्नात्वा स्नात्वा प्रयत्नतः ..
6.2.m: Taking water from the Śiprā, bathing [the liṅga] again and again with effort,
until the water came again to the Śiprā, O dear one. .. 43 ..
In the meantime, from it there arose a dense mass of smoke,
vast and filled with wreaths of flames from the middle of the liṅga, O fair-hipped one! .. 44 ..
Then everything visible in the sky became blazing with fire;
by the multitude of its flames, the orb of the planets was burned .. 45 ..
as far as the path of the lunar mansions. Terrified by that, O dear one,
the planets, their faces overcome by smoke and flames, sought refuge in that very [liṅga]. .. 46 ..

6.2.s: tato brahmā ca viṣṇuśca taddṛṣṭvā mahadadbhutam ..
6.2.d: ततो ब्रह्मा च विष्णुश्च तद्दृष्ट्वा महदद्भुतम् ..
6.2.m: Then Brahmā and Viṣṇu, seeing that great wonder,
and the thousand-eyed Indra surrounded by the gods, approached the vicinity of the liṅga. .. 47 ..
That liṅga had mighty flames, filling the sky with fiery tongues;

6.2.s: duḥprekṣyaṃ durvidaṃ bhīmaṃ varddhamānaṃ dadarśa saḥ .. 48 ..
6.2.d: दुःप्रेक्ष्यं दुर्विदं भीमं वर्द्धमानं ददर्श सः .. 48 ..
6.2.m: he beheld it growing, difficult to look upon, incomprehensible, and terrifying. .. 48 ..
In the mere twinkling of an eye, it grew ten thousand yojanas.
Beholding the most wondrous form of that growing liṅga,
the lord of the gods fell into delusion, and the planets then lost consciousness. .. 49 ..
Then from that liṅga, streams of water gushed forth;
from one part [of it], O fair-hipped one, the earth was turned into a single ocean. .. 50 ..
From another part of the liṅga arose a mighty wind,
and in another region appeared a mass of lightnings. .. 51 ..
A smoky flame burst forth from yet another region of the liṅga. .. 52 ..
Having thus seen that most wondrous unmanifest liṅga
growing on every side, arisen and filling the expanse of the sky, .. 53 ..
the planets became bewildered, their senses agitated by the smoke.
Being scorched all around, they then praised the liṅga: .. 54 ..
.. The planets said ..
"Salutations to the one of beautiful form, worshipped by the gods; salutations to the one whose nature and action are manifold.
Salutations, salutations to the one free from physical form; to the one whose form is water, salutations, salutations to you! .. 55 ..

6.2.s: iti stuto yadā devi grahaiḥ krūraistadā priye ..
6.2.d: इति स्तुतो यदा देवि ग्रहैः क्रूरैस्तदा प्रिये ..
6.2.m: When praised in this manner by the cruel planets, O goddess, then, O dear one,
there manifested from the liṅga, standing in the sky, His true form in embodied shape: .. 56 ..
his whole body grey with ashes, radiant with armlets made of the coils of serpents,
resembling a mass of snow, stainless as a silver mountain.
And he spoke to these planets, who bowed low with trembling necks: .. 57 ..

6.2.s: kiṃ vā kāmaṃ mano'bhīṣṭaṃ bhavadbhyo yaddadāmyaham ..
6.2.d: किं वा कामं मनोऽभीष्टं भवद्भ्यो यद्ददाम्यहम् ..
6.2.m: "What desired wish in your hearts may I grant to you?
All this is not in vain, and my darśana is exceedingly difficult to attain." .. 58 ..
I grant [my] darśana indeed to you for the satisfaction of the world."
Having spoken thus, all the planets then said with joined palms: 59

6.2.s: yadi deyo varo deva yadi tuṣṭo'si śaṃkara ..
6.2.d: यदि देयो वरो देव यदि तुष्टोऽसि शंकर ..
6.2.m: "If a boon is to be given, O God, if you are pleased, O Śaṃkara,

6.2.s: karmāraṃbheṣu sarveṣu pūjā' smākaṃ yathā bhavet ..
6.2.d: कर्मारंभेषु सर्वेषु पूजा' स्माकं यथा भवेत् ..
6.2.m: act so, O Mahādeva, that at the beginning of all undertakings
our worship shall take place; through that there will be satisfaction." 60
Having said, "So it shall be," he then addressed the cloud Uttara:

6.2.s: tuṣṭo'smyahaṃ tu te vatsa gṛhāṇa varamīpsitam .. 61 ..
6.2.d: तुष्टोऽस्म्यहं तु ते वत्स गृहाण वरमीप्सितम् .. 61 ..
6.2.m: "I am well pleased with you, dear child; choose the boon you desire." 61

6.2.s: tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tatra hyuttaraḥ prāha harṣitaḥ ..
6.2.d: तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तत्र ह्युत्तरः प्राह हर्षितः ..
6.2.m: Hearing that speech there, Uttara, delighted, spoke:
"Since you are pleased with me, O Lord, grant me this boon: 62
Whenever anyone causes us great distress,

6.2.s: tadā vṛṣṭirvidhātabyā tvayā deva sadā bhuvi .. 63 ..
6.2.d: तदा वृष्टिर्विधातब्या त्वया देव सदा भुवि .. 63 ..
6.2.m: then rain must always be produced by you on earth, O God. 63

6.2.s: rakṣā kāryā ca meghānāṃ rakṣaṇīyāstvayā vayam..
6.2.d: रक्षा कार्या च मेघानां रक्षणीयास्त्वया वयम्..
6.2.m: Protection must be granted to the clouds, and we must be protected by you."
O daughter of the mountain's frame, the liṅga said to him, "So be it! 64

6.2.s: adyaprabhṛti te nāmnā khyātiṃ yāsyāmi bhūtale...
6.2.d: अद्यप्रभृति ते नाम्ना ख्यातिं यास्यामि भूतले...
6.2.m: From this day forward I shall attain renown on earth by your name;
I shall become known as Uttareśvara, there is no doubt. 65

6.2.s: ye māṃ saṃpūjayiṣyaṃti bhaktyā paramayā yutāḥ ..
6.2.d: ये मां संपूजयिष्यंति भक्त्या परमया युताः ..
6.2.m: Those who will worship me endowed with supreme devotion,
to them I shall continuously grant the fruit of their desired aims on earth. 66

6.2.s: paśyaṃti prayatā ye māṃ kṛtvā niyamapūrvakam ..
6.2.d: पश्यंति प्रयता ये मां कृत्वा नियमपूर्वकम् ..
6.2.m: Those restrained persons who behold me following observances,
they shall go to Śiva's city for eight myriad kalpas, 67
mounted upon sun-like aerial chariots fulfilling all wishes,
thronged with maidens of Rudra, accompanied by swans and cranes, 68
resounding with dance and instruments, echoing with loud music,
being fanned [with chowries] by men, praised by gods and asuras. 69
Even one devoid of devotion who beholds me incidentally without deceit,
to him I will grant sovereignty in the northern Kurus. 70

6.2.s: smariṣyati ca yo nityaṃ prabhāte cottareśvaram ..
6.2.d: स्मरिष्यति च यो नित्यं प्रभाते चोत्तरेश्वरम् ..
6.2.m: And whoever constantly remembers Uttareśvara at dawn,
he goes to the supreme abode free from burning and dissolution. 71

6.2.s: eṣa te kathito devi prabhāvaḥ pāpanāśanaḥ ..
6.2.d: एष ते कथितो देवि प्रभावः पापनाशनः ..
6.2.m: This power that destroys sins has been told to you, O Goddess,
pertaining to the god Uttareśvara; now hear of Trilocaneśvara." 72

6.2.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे चतुरशीतिलिङ्गमाहात्म्य उत्तरेश्वरमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम चतुश्चत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः .. 44 ..
6.2.m: Thus ends the forty-fourth chapter, named "Description of the Greatness of Uttareśvara," in the Greatness of the Eighty-Four Liṅgas, in the fifth section Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses. 44

6.2.m: The god of gods said: / Know the forty-fifth deity to be Trilocaneśvara, / by the mere darśana of whom all perfection is attained. 1 / There was an ancient history here, at the sacred base named Virajas, / in the temple of Trilocana made of gems and rubies, 2 / rich in windows of various shapes, like another peak of jewels, / adorned with a radiant golden finial, 3 / upon which the full moon sat as if from weariness. / There a pair of pigeons, having made their abode, lived at will, 4 / constantly circumambulating in the morning, evening, and at noon, / flying all around, driving away in all ten directions / the dust clinging to the temple with the gusts from their wings. / The name "Trilocana" and likewise "Triviṣṭapa" / constantly uttered by devotees became a guest to their ears. 6 / The four kinds of instruments that thoroughly delight Śambhu, / reaching the hollows of their ears, produced echoes. 7 / The light of the auspicious waving lamps at the three junctures of day, constantly entering the corners of the eyes of those two birds, / revealed the devotion of the devotees. 8 / Even setting aside their search for sustenance, their minds steady at times, / not flying away to their desired place, the two birds remained watching the spectacle. 9 / Picking up rice and other grains around the temple / that was constantly thronged with people on the ground, they performed circumambulations. 10 / In the southern quarter of the god, being afflicted with thirst, / they constantly drank the water born of Viṣṇu's body, and after bathing, they would return. 11 / As they were thus moving about in the vicinity of Trilocana, / much time passed for the two birds of noble conduct. 12 / Then, as they were perched inside a window on the temple's shoulder, comfortably seated, / they were seen with a cruel gaze by a certain hawk. 13 / Wishing to seize that pair of pigeons, / the hawk quickly descended from the sky and perched upon Śiva's temple. 14 / Then he watched their arrival and departure: / by what difficult path the birds entered, 15 / and by what road they came out, at what time, and what they were doing; / "How can these two be seized by me simultaneously at will? 16 / Even a weak enemy cannot be overcome suddenly. / Not even with a thousand elephants and a hundred thousand noble horses / can a deed of a king be accomplished that is achieved by a single fortress. / An enemy stationed in a fortress cannot be defeated anywhere by anyone, / if the fortress is independent and reveals false paths." 18 / Thus praising the strength in a fortress, his eyes red with rage, / seeing the two cooing birds fearless, the hawk departed into the courtyard of the sky. 19 / Then the clever female pigeon, seeing the destruction of her enemy / through the strength of the fortress, spoke to her pigeon husband, the mighty one: 20 / The cooing female said: / "O dear pigeon, O wise one, producer of the sounds of all pleasures of love, / this hawk, a powerful enemy, has come into your sight." 21 / Hearing those words of the female pigeon, the good husband / said this to the female pigeon: "Why this worry of yours, my dear? 22

The pigeon said:
"How many sky-farers indeed are there not here, O lovely one?
How many birds do not live in temples and other buildings? 23
And how many do not see the two of us dwelling comfortably here, my dear?
If we were to fear them here, whence would come that happiness of ours, my dear? 24

Having heard these words from the noble pigeon, the female pigeon

with an unwavering gaze, like Death looking upon one whose lifespan has expired.
Then, as he circled the palace in circular flight,
the beloved female said: “Lord, did you see that wicked enemy?
