6.2.m:
The venerable Hara said:
Know the seventy-fourth Śiva to be Rājasthaleśvara,
merely by whose darśana one is released from all sins. (1)
Formerly, when the Viṣṇukalpa had occurred, pleasing to the beginning of the Manvantara,
when the earth’s surface was without a king, Brahmā became filled with anxiety: (2)
“Without human beings, the gods are unable to sustain the worlds;
from gifts, sacrifices, and recitations, the gods enjoy supreme nourishment. (3)
Who could be a fit king, a protector of subjects, fond of the people?”
He then saw the royal sage Ripuñjaya performing austerity (4)
on earth, endowed with every virtue, devoted to dharma, of great vows.
Then the Lord of the gods, Brahmā, grandfather of the worlds, said to him: (5)
Brahmā said:
Ripuñjaya, heed this word of mine, my child;
and let the kingdom be protected, dear son, with a resolute mind. (6)
Enough of your austerity now, my child, with this hardship;
all the worlds have been conquered through dharma by you, best of men. (7)
Now let the protection of the world be carried out at my command,
for indeed benevolence toward others is the fruit of having an embodied form. (8)
There is no other dharma like that, nor anything else that accomplishes wealth;
even attainment of hell is better, if one has benefited another. (9)
Not by harming beings should there be sovereignty over the earth.
Constantly, for the sake of the affairs of the world, and out of respect for my command,
protect the earth, whose garment is the ocean, and the subjects as well. (10)
Thus addressed by Brahmā, O daughter of the mountain,
that royal sage Ripuñjaya, joining his palms, said to Brahmā: (11)
“By nature the earth was formerly fashioned motionless by you;
without a protector, indeed, where will this earth go? (12)
If the earth must certainly be protected by me, O Grandfather,
then give me the charming city of Avantī, which endures for seven kalpas. (13)
It is renowned in the entire world of mortals as comparable to Amarāvatī,
established as a dwelling for the gods fallen from heaven. (14)
If the dwellers of heaven will abide by my decree,
and without my grant no one will have a residence [there],
then by this rule I will protect the earth, O Lord.” (15)
Brahmā said:
“This desire of yours that you have spoken shall come to pass, best of men.
Whatever gods there are, out of respect for me,
they will execute your command, always subject to your authority. (16)
And your name will indeed be Devanātha, O you of noble vows.”
Having said this, Brahmā, mounted on his swan vehicle, vanished. (17)
Then the king, having promised the protection of the earth to Brahmā,
proclaimed on earth, and spoke to the dwellers of heaven: (18)
“Heaven has been designated for you, and the surface of the earth for mortals;
and those gods who dwell here, engaged in caves, or on the ground, or on mountains— (19)
let them depart; this earth belongs to mortals.”
Hearing that proclamation of his, afflicted with fear,
the gods, because of Brahmā’s words and out of respect, went to heaven. (20)
Then that king fostered the subjects through dharma at that time,
and they were exceedingly delighted by his heart filled with affection as for a son. (21)

6.2.m: The subjects, thriving in that happiness, were free from old age and death, / blessed with sons, rich in wealth and grain, endowed with all desires, / in the prime of youth, free from dualities, and constantly devoted to righteousness. / There was on earth no mountain, dry high ground, or island [left barren]; / the earth brought forth crops without cultivation and was laden with delicious fruits. / The earth became like the realm of the gods, resplendent with the qualities of all desires. / As time passed in this manner, while the king was ruling his realm, / the gods, consumed with great jealousy, strove to hinder his affairs. / They repeatedly inflicted manifold miseries upon the subjects; / then Pākaśāsana caused an exceedingly long drought. / When the worlds were thus being ruined, that best of kings, / having become a cloud, went to the sky and produced abundant rain. / Refreshed by that alone, the people became happy, O illustrious lady! / Then at a certain time, as Pākaśāsana poured down rain, / having become the Samvartaka storm cloud, he cast down torrential rains. / Then, having become the wind, the king held it back. / Then fire vanished everywhere from the face of the earth: / neither sacrifices, nor silent prayers, nor oblations, nor cooking took place, / and the world, afflicted with disease, was thrown into dire distress. / Then that king, seeing this, became the bearer of oblations himself; / he sustained all the subjects and the sacrifices of the heaven-dwellers. / In the meantime, O goddess, I came together with you / to see his city, accompanied by the host of spirits. / Then all the hosts of gods, along with kinnaras and great serpents, / with yakṣas, rākṣasas, and gandharvas, with siddhas, vidyādharas, and serpents, / bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, and whatever others roam the sky; / the four oceans as well, the salt sea, milk ocean, and the rest; / the Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sindhu, Candrabhāgā, Sarasvatī, / Carmaṇvatī, Bhīmarathī, and the holy Godāvarī river; / Vipāśā, the holy Devikā, Śarayū, and Kauśikī; / Gomatī, Dhūtapāpā, Bāhudā, and Dṛṣadvatī; / Pārā, Veda, Smṛti, Vetraghnī, the auspicious Narmadā, / Tāpī, Payoṣṇī, and Nirvindhyā—all arrived there; / Puṣkara, Prayāga, Prabhāsa, and Naimiṣa; / Pṛthūtaka, and likewise Amarakaṇṭaka; / Gaṅgādvāra, Kuśāvarta, Bilvaka, Nīlaparvata, / Vārāhaparvata, and the tīrtha Kanakhala; / Bhṛgutuṅga, Sukukṣa, and Ajagandha, O Pārvatī; / Kāliñjara with Kedāra, Rudrakoṭi, and Mahālaya; / and all holy sites and shrines; / Meru, Mahendra, Malaya, Mandara, Gandhamādana; / the sages, the Vālakhilyas, and the four Vedas— / these and many others arrived along with me. / Thereupon, Meru was fashioned by me into the form of a plateau. / Situated on that plateau, O goddess, I sat surrounded by the gods; / stationed at my side were the four oceans, beginning with the salt sea. / Then that king Ripuñjaya fell into agitation; / seeing me seated on his plateau, he approached me. / Though scorched by my splendor, O fair-faced lady, / and though frightened, he pleased me [saying]: “Who are you, O god? Homage to you!” / “O king, on this plateau I am king,” I too said playfully. / “The king is the fourfold ends of life, the fourfold form, situated in four ways.” / By him I was perceived everywhere in whatever is endowed with speech, moving and unmoving; / thereafter, he praised me with supreme devotion, O beloved! / Seeing my matchless and supreme all-pervading power, / with supreme devotion, O goddess, he sought refuge with me. / As he praised me repeatedly, I was indeed pleased with that lord of the earth. / By him it was said: “If you are pleased with me, O god, supreme lord:

Īśvara said: / Know the seventy-fifth god, named Vaḍaleśvara, O goddess, / to be the remover of sins and the grantor of desires to mortals upon seeing [him]. 1
O goddess, Dhanada had a friend named Maṇibhadra.
His son was Vaḍala, wrathful and powerful through jealousy, 2
handsome, constantly lustful, ever intoxicated, and exceedingly strong.
Once he went to the lovely lotus pond belonging to Dhanada, 3
hidden and constructed in secret for sexual pleasure and indulgence in passion.
He saw it covered with blossoms and adorned with diamonds and cat's-eye gems, 4
indeed strewn with coral, radiant with pearl garlands, 5
delightful, casting extensive shade, adorned with golden lotuses,
close to Kubera's mansion and beloved of Dhanada, 6
the pleasure-garden of the high-souled Kubera, the king of kings,
guarded constantly by sword-bearing rākṣasas and kiṃnaras.
Having seen it, Vaḍala was then filled with great delight. 7
Accompanied by his beloved, he dallied in that secret, charming place;

Guarding that place were brave rākṣasas, skilled in battle;

Upon seeing Vaḍala, the son of Maṇibhadra, O dear one—
his mouth filled with delicacies, adorned with celestial sandalwood, 10
his mouth most splendid with teeth resembling the inner petals of the ketakī,
bearing a strapped sword for battle, endowed with power, a conqueror of foes, 11
accompanied by his wife, intoxicated, ever resting upon a couch—
and realizing he had come for love-making, they shouted to one another: 12
"Do not, O warrior, proceed along this path with your wife!
This is the pleasure-garden of Kubera, the high-souled Dhanada. 13
Gods, divine seers, yakṣas, gandharvas, and kiṃnaras,
having asked the foremost yakṣa, wander about and dally here. 14
It is not possible to stroll and play here long without permission,
whether by a brother, a minister, a friend, or even by a son. 15

"Seize him! Bind him! Cut him to pieces! Let us drink [his blood] and devour this immoral one!"
So saying in rage, with rolling eyes, they swiftly rushed forward, raising their weapons. 19
Then he, seizing a heavy, great mace bound with golden plates, / resembling the rod of Yama,
the swift hero charged at them, and shouted: "Halt, halt!" 20
Beholding his valor and power, as well as the power of his science and the strength of his arms,
the assembled warriors were unable to withstand him; struck down, the foremost heroes suddenly turned back. 21
Being torn to pieces, their senses bewildered, they swiftly flew into the sky from that very place;

6.2.s:
kailāsaśṛṃgāṇyabhi dudruvuste yakṣārditā rakṣapālāḥ prabhagnāḥ .. 22 ..

patito bhūtale caiva tasminsthāne gato'pi san .. 28 ..

6.2.d:
कैलासशृंगाण्यभि दुद्रुवुस्ते यक्षार्दिता रक्षपालाः प्रभग्नाः .. 22 ..
स शक्रवद्दानवदैत्यसंघान्विक्रम्य जित्वा मदनाभितप्तः ..
विगाह्य तां पुष्करिणीं समर्थः कामं स चिक्रीडति यक्षपुत्रः .. 23 ..
ततस्तु ते रक्षपालाः समेत्य धनेश्वरं वै वडलेन नुन्नाः ..
यक्षस्य धैर्यं सुबलं च संख्ये यथावदाचख्युरतीव भीताः .. .. 24 ..
तेषां तु वचनं श्रुत्वा मणिभद्रो महायशाः ..
शशाप पुत्रं दयितं वडलं प्रभुकारणात् .. 25 ..
यस्मात्सा नलिनी रम्या सेविता वडलेन तु..
दयिता धनदस्यापि यथा माता तथैव सा ..26..
तस्मात्पुत्रो मदीयस्तु सर्वभागविवर्जितः..
पंग्वन्धो बधिरो दीनः क्षयरोगमवाप्स्यति.. .. 27 ..
इति शप्तस्तदा जातो वडलो भोगवर्जितः ..
पतितो भूतले चैव तस्मिन्स्थाने गतोऽपि सन् .. 28 ..
पीडितः क्षयरोगेण न शशाक विचेष्टितुम् ..
6.2.m:
afflicted by the yakṣa, the routed guards of the demon king fled toward the peaks of Kailāsa. 22
Having displayed prowess and conquered [them] like Indra [conquering] hordes of Dānavas and Daityas,
the capable son of the yakṣa, burning with love, plunged into that lotus pond and sportively played as he pleased. 23
Then those guards, assembled and driven away by Vaḍala,
terrified indeed, truthfully reported to the Lord of Wealth the yakṣa's courage and great strength in battle. 24
Hearing their words, the illustrious Maṇibhadra
cursed his beloved son Vaḍala for the sake of his master: 25
"Because that delightful lotus pond was used by Vaḍala—
one that is beloved of Dhanada, and therefore like a mother— 26
therefore, this son of mine, deprived of all wealth and share,
crippled, blind, deaf, and wretched, shall contract consumption." 27
Thus cursed, Vaḍala was then deprived of pleasures;
even though he had reached that place, he fell to the surface of the earth. 28
Afflicted by consumption, he was unable to move.

andho'tha badhiro jāto guruśāpahatastadā .. 29 ..

6.2.d:
अन्धोऽथ बधिरो जातो गुरुशापहतस्तदा .. 29 ..
चिंतयामास सहसा शापमत्यद्भुतं महत् ..
शप्तोऽहं केन सहसा जीवन्योन्यंतरं गतः .. 5.2.75.30 ..
कथं शप्तोऽस्मि तातेन मणिभद्रेण वल्लभः ..
पुत्रो युवा च शूरश्च शत्रुपक्षक्षयंकरः .. 31 ..
धन्योऽसौ मणिभद्रोऽपि मत्तातो येन भूतले ..
प्रभुभक्त्या निजः पुत्रः शप्तस्त्यक्तश्च तत्क्षणात् .. 32 ..
वडलेन पुनः प्रोक्तं धन्योऽहं प्रभुकारणात्..
उत्सवो निधनंनाम भर्तृपिण्डोपजीविनाम् .. 33 ..
अन्यायेन यथाकामं प्रारब्धः संचितश्चिरम्..
तेनाहं शापतां प्राप्तो यास्यामि नरकं ध्रुवम्.. 34 ..
एवं विलपतस्तस्य वडलस्य वरानने ..
आजगाम तमुद्देशं मणिभद्रो महाबलः ..
ददर्श पुत्रं पंग्वंधं क्षयरोगप्रपीडितम् .. 35 ..
निःश्वसंतं सुदुःखार्त्तं विल पंतं पुनःपुनः ..
6.2.m:
Then, struck by his elder's curse, he became blind and deaf. // 29
Suddenly he reflected upon this terrible, exceedingly strange curse:
“By whom was I suddenly cursed, passing alive into another state? // 5.2.75.30
How was I cursed by my father, Maṇibhadra—I, his beloved
son, young, heroic, and the destroyer of enemy factions? // 31
Blessed indeed is that Maṇibhadra, my father, by whom on earth
his own son was cursed and instantly abandoned out of devotion to his master! // 32 //”
Vaḍala spoke again: “Blessed am I for my master's sake!
For those who subsist on their master's food, death itself is a festive occasion. // 33
Unjustly and at my own pleasure, [this crime] was begun and amassed for a long time;
by that I have attained this curse, and I shall surely go to hell.” // 34
As that Vaḍala was thus lamenting, O fair-faced one,
the mighty Maṇibhadra came to that place.
He saw his son lame, blind, and tormented by consumption, // 35
sighing deeply, afflicted with great sorrow, and wailing again and again.

6.2.s:
pratyuvāca sutaṃ yakṣo maṇibhadro'tiduḥkhitaḥ ..

tvayeyaṃ nalinī ramyā dhana dasyātivallabhā ..
sevitā kāmataptena pravarā rākṣasā hatāḥ .. 37 ..

6.2.d:
प्रत्युवाच सुतं यक्षो मणिभद्रोऽतिदुःखितः ..
मया कुपित्रा हा वत्स शप्तस्त्वं प्रभुकारणात् .. 36 ..
त्वयेयं नलिनी रम्या धन दस्यातिवल्लभा ..
सेविता कामतप्तेन प्रवरा राक्षसा हताः .. 37 ..
तस्मात्पुत्र मया शप्तो न मिथ्या स भविष्यति ..
प्रभुर्देवः प्रभुः स्वामी प्रभुर्माता प्रभुः पिता .. 38 ..
स्वाम्यर्थे यः प्रियान्प्राणान्परित्यजति संगरे ..
स याति परमं स्थानं ब्रह्मलोकं सनातनम्.. 39 ..
न मन्त्रसाध्यः शापोयं नौषधेन व्रतेन च ..
नियमेन च दानेन तस्मान्मद्वचनं कुरु .. 5.2.75.40 ..
मया श्रुतं शक्रलोके पुराणं स्कंदकीर्त्तितम् ..
ब्रुवतो नारदस्यैव देवानां संनिधौ पुरा .. 41 ..
प्रभावो वर्णितस्तेन महाकालवनस्य च ..
क्षेत्रे ह्यस्मिन्महालिंगं स्वर्गद्वारस्य दक्षिणे .. 42 ..
विद्यते व्याधिशमनं रूपसौभाग्यदायकम् ..
6.2.m:
The yakṣa Maṇibhadra, exceedingly grieved, replied to his son:
“Alas, my child! By me, a bad father, you were cursed for the master’s sake! // 36
This delightful lotus pond, so dear to Dhanada,
was enjoyed by you, tormented by passion, and excellent rākṣasas were slain. // 37
Therefore, O son, you were cursed by me, and it cannot prove false.
The master is a god, the master is the lord, the master is mother, and the master is father. // 38
He who relinquishes his dear life in battle for the sake of his master
goes to the supreme abode, the eternal world of Brahmā. // 39
This curse cannot be counteracted by mantras, nor by medicine, nor by vow,
nor by discipline or gifts; therefore do what I say. // 5.2.75.40
In the realm of Śakra, I heard the Purāṇa proclaimed by Skanda,
as Nārada himself was reciting it long ago in the presence of the gods. // 41
By him was described the power of the forest of Mahākāla:
in this sacred field, south of Svargadvāra, there is a great liṅga // 42
which cures disease and bestows beauty and good fortune.

6.2.d:
तत्राहं त्वां च नेष्यामि विमानेनाशुगामिना .. 43 ..
इत्युक्त्वा मणिभद्रेण समानीतः सुतस्तदा ..
यत्र देवाधिदेवोऽसौ स्वर्गद्वारस्य दक्षिणे.. 44 ..
स्पर्शनात्तस्य लिंगस्य चक्षुष्मान्रूपवान्बली ..
सुपादः श्रुतिसंयुक्तस्तत्क्षणादभवत्तदा ..45..
दृष्ट्वा सुमहदाश्चर्यं मणिभद्रेण पार्वति..
कृतं नाम सुहृष्टेन स्वीयपुत्रस्य नामतः..
चक्षुष्मान्वडलो जातो लिंगस्यास्य प्रभावतः..46..
अद्यप्रभृति देवोऽयं वडलेश्वरसंज्ञकः..
भविष्यति त्रिलोकेषु विख्यातो नेत्रदायकः..47..
पूजयिष्यंति ये देवं वडलेश्वरसंज्ञकम्..
लिंगं लोकेषु विख्यातं ते प्राप्स्यंति मनोरथम्..48..
दृष्टो हरति पापानि स्पृष्टो राज्यं प्रयच्छति..
अर्चितो भक्तिभावेन मोक्षं दद्यान्न संशयः..49..
कार्त्तिके शुक्लपक्षस्य तिथिर्वै द्वादशी भवेत् ..
तस्यां ये पूजयिष्यंति वडलेश्वरसंज्ञकम् ..5.2.75.50 ..
6.2.m:
There I will take you in a swift-flying aerial chariot.” // 43
Having said this, his son was then brought by Maṇibhadra
to where that God of gods resides, south of Svargadvāra. // 44
From touching that liṅga, he instantly became endowed with sight,
handsome, strong, with sound feet, and endowed with hearing. // 45
Having seen this great wonder, O Pārvatī,
Maṇibhadra, overjoyed, gave it a name after the name of his own son:
“Vaḍala gained his sight through the power of this liṅga. // 46
From this day forth, this god named Vaḍaleśvara
shall become renowned in the three worlds as the giver of eyes. // 47
Those who worship this god named Vaḍaleśvara,
this liṅga renowned across the worlds, will obtain their heart's desire. // 48
Beheld, it removes sins; touched, it grants sovereignty;
worshiped with devotion, it grants liberation beyond doubt. // 49
Whenever the twelfth lunar day of the bright fortnight in the month of Kārttika occurs,
those who worship on that day [the deity] named Vaḍaleśvara, // 5.2.75.50

गर्भवासे न जायंते सर्वसौख्यसमन्विताः .. 52 ..
गाणपत्या भविष्यंति शंकरस्य सदा प्रियाः ..
सौभाग्यरूपसंपन्नाः पुत्रपौत्रैश्च संयुताः ..
जायंते मानवा लोके वडलेश्वरदर्शनात् .. 53 ..
गर्भवासे महाकष्टे यस्य वासो न रोचते ..
सोऽभ्यर्चयतु भावेन वडलेश्वरमीश्वरम् .. 54 ..

इत्युक्त्वा मणिभद्रोऽपि सुतेन सहितो ययौ ..

6.2.m:
have constantly given gifts; they go to the supreme abode.
At Prayāga, at Prabhāsa, and at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean, // 51
austerity has indeed been practiced by them; they are liberated, there is no doubt here.
They are never born into the womb, and they are endowed with all happiness. // 52
They shall become leaders of the gaṇas, ever dear to Śaṃkara;
endowed with good fortune and beauty, and blessed with sons and grandsons,
humans are born in the world from having the darśana of Vaḍaleśvara. // 53
He who does not delight in living within the womb, which is full of great misery,
should worship the lord Vaḍaleśvara with deep devotion. // 54
Without the liṅga there is no perfection; the supreme abode is hard to attain.
No access to heaven comes to pass as long as one does not worship the liṅga. // 55
For those devoid of liṅga worship, spiritual success is exceedingly hard to attain,
since the desired goal was obtained by my son from the liṅga.” // 56
Having said this, Maṇibhadra departed together with his son.
where the god presiding over wealth went to his supreme abode.

6.2.m: Thus ends the second [part], the Glory of the Eighty-Four Liṅgas Situated in Avantī, in the fifth Avantī Section of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa.
